Compose stack plus the overview docs for GRANDstack (GraphQL on Neo4j: `grandstack-server`, `grandstack-web`). Read [docs/agents.md](/docs/grandstack/agents/) first; it covers the mental model, where to change what, the verification checklist and the gotchas. [llms.txt](https://github.com/grand-stack/grandstack/blob/main/llms.txt) indexes everything.

- **Build on the blocks; do not make a silo.** A new repository or setup must be made from what GRANDstack already provides (the `grandstack-server` image and its models, the `grandstack-federation` gateway, `grandstack-auth`, `grandstack-agents`, compose overlays in the `grandstack` repository), and improve a block when it falls short rather than copying or working around it. Read [building on GRANDstack](/docs/grandstack/building-on-grandstack/) before creating a repository, a compose file, a server, a gateway or a docs structure. Providing building blocks that people shape into their own solution is a goal of the project.
- Start: `cp .env.example .env && docker compose up --build` (web :3000, GraphQL :4000/graphql, Neo4j :7474). The three repos must sit side by side because compose builds from `../grandstack-server` and `../grandstack-web`.
- `docker compose down -v` deletes the Neo4j data; the sample reseeds on the next start.
- Change the schema, seed or server behaviour in `grandstack-server`; change the UI in `grandstack-web`; follow each repo's `AGENTS.md` and `docs/recipes.md`.
- Before you finish, run the checks for each repo you changed (listed in [docs/agents.md](/docs/grandstack/agents/#verification-checklist)) and `node scripts/check-links.mjs` here.
- The default stack has no authentication. The opt-in auth setup (`docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.auth.yaml up --build`, from the `grandstack-auth` repo) is development-only. Do not expose either publicly.
- Agents: `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.agents.yaml up --build` adds an MCP server at http://localhost:4100/mcp (from the `grandstack-agents` repo). It is read-only unless `AGENTS_ALLOW_MUTATIONS=true`, has no auth of its own, and talks to the open server. Keep it local.
- Federation: `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.federation.yaml up --build` (from the `grandstack-federation` repo) puts a gateway on :4000 and moves the server subgraph to :4001; a Wikipedia subgraph adds summaries to films and people. Needs internet. It replaces the other setups on port 4000. Open, no auth.
- Aura management: `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.aura.yaml up --build` (from the `grandstack-web-aura` repo; needs `SECRET_KEY` in `.env`, made by that repo's `scripts/init-env.sh`) replaces the Movies app with a web UI for managing Neo4j Aura. The server runs with `MODEL=aura` (read-only, and a writable copy on a private network for the Aura subgraph), the gateway is the federation image with that repo's config, and it talks to the REAL Aura API by default (`-f compose.aura-mock.yaml` adds a fake one for tests and fixes the address to it). Everything is bound to loopback. It replaces the other setups on ports 3000 and 4000 and uses its own Neo4j volume. Never run `down -v` under the default project name beside a Movies stack you want to keep (use `-p aura`). `compose.aura-edge.yaml` adds TLS and a sign-in.
- Keep docs true: update the doc next to the behaviour you change, in the same change.
- Diagrams: `docs/diagrams/*.svg` are hand-written SVG with numbered callouts, each embedded with a numbered text legend. When you change the behaviour a diagram shows, edit the SVG and its legend in the same change; `node scripts/check-links.mjs` fails if an image has no alt text, an SVG contains script or style, or the legend numbers differ from the callouts drawn.

- New code files need the copyright header (two lines: `Copyright (c) "Neo4j"` and `Neo4j Sweden AB [http://neo4j.com]`, in the file's comment syntax). Run `node ../grandstack/scripts/add-headers.mjs` to add it everywhere; `--check` lists what is missing. Generated files are exempt.
- Releases use the **release-cut** workflow (Actions tab), which sets the version in every `package.json`, tags and publishes. Do not bump versions or push tags by hand; see `grandstack/docs/releasing.md`.
- Base images in Dockerfiles and compose files are pinned to an exact version **and** a digest (`image:1.2.3@sha256:...`), never a floating tag such as `latest` or `24-slim`, so a rebuilt image cannot silently change or be swapped. Dependabot proposes updates to both; take them through a pull request that passes CI. To pin a new image, look up the digest of the multi-arch index (not of one platform).
